messages:
alice_support: Hey @customer_acme — I saw your ticket about 413s when sending large embedding batches. Can you paste the failing request (no secrets) and the exact error body?

customer_acme: hitting 413 Payload Too Large. sending ~40k vectors in one JSON POST to /v1/embeddings. error: 
{
  "status":413,
  "message":"request payload too large"
}

alice_support: thanks. two quick things: which model (dim) and approx payload size in bytes? also are you using streaming/chunked upload or one big JSON array?

customer_acme: model is "text-embed-ada-002" (1536 dim). sending one big JSON array of vectors. payload file size ~ 25MB before gzip. using node fetch + JSON.stringify(data) and POST.

dev_jordan: fwiw, float32 1536 dims ~ 6KB per vector raw, plus JSON overhead. 40k vectors x ~6KB = ~240MB raw, JSON can be much bigger. 25MB sounds small for 40k, are you sending tokenized floats or strings?

customer_acme: oh sorry typo — 4k vectors, not 40k. still big.

alice_support: OK that aligns. gateway limits typically hit around 8–10MB for a single request depending on proxy. 413 = request rejected by some layer (NGINX/edge) before backend. we should confirm exact cutoff.

sre_liz: confirmed infra: our edge proxy currently enforces 10MB max body. payload over that triggers 413. backend also imposes memory budget which can 500/raid. we log a 413 at the gateway level.

customer_acme: any workaround? we need to embed 4k items every hour.

alice_support: immediate options:
- client-side chunking: send smaller batches (we recommend <=500 vectors for 1536-dim models to keep JSON payloads ~3–5MB).
- streaming/multipart: upload vectors to a blob store (S3) and send a reference to process server-side (we don't currently support pull-from-s3 in the hosted embeddings endpoint; ops flow required).
- gzip: compressing JSON can help but not reliable if proxy uncompresses. better to chunk.

dev_jordan: adding an example chunker (Node) — this is what we use in SDKs. chunk size tuned for model dims and observed JSON overhead:

```js
async function* chunkVectors(vectors, chunkSize = 500){
  for (let i = 0; i < vectors.length; i += chunkSize){
    yield vectors.slice(i, i + chunkSize);
  }
}

for await (const chunk of chunkVectors(allVectors, 500)) {
  await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <KEY>', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'text-embed-ada-002', input: chunk })
  });
}
```

alice_support: also include exponential backoff and idempotency key if you need de-dup on retries.

customer_acme: what about the dimension mismatch errors we sometimes see when chunking? e.g. we get 400/422 "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768" on some requests.

dev_jordan: that usually means mixed inputs or using the wrong model param in some chunks. common causes:
- an earlier preprocessing step returned lower-dim vectors (e.g., encoding step failed or different encoder)
- sending previously stored embeddings (already floats) instead of raw text to embeddings endpoint (we expect raw text inputs for model to produce embeddings)
- JSON encoding problems truncating arrays so model sees wrong length

sre_liz: repro checklist we ask for:
1) exact request body (first failing chunk)
2) Content-Length of request (from client logs)
3) gateway logs showing 413 or backend logs showing 422
4) model param in each chunk request

customer_acme: attaching small repro. first chunk body ~4.2MB. second chunk 6.8MB -> second got 413.

alice_support: that tracks. for the 422 dimension case please confirm you're not POSTing precomputed vectors. error looks like backend validating dims and returning 422. sample error body we've seen: 
{
  "error": "Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768"
}

ops_patch: note: if the client sends arrays of numbers (i.e., already-embedded vectors) our endpoint expects a different primitive schema and may reject or mis-interpret. Please confirm input shape matches docs: input should be array of strings (or array of objects with "input").

dev_jordan: small repro pattern we suggest:
1) run a local generator to chunk with size cap by bytes, not count. Example pseudo:
```js
// estimate bytes per item and pick chunkSize so totalUtf8Bytes < 5_000_000
let chunk = []; let chunkBytes = 0;
for (const item of inputs) {
  const b = Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(item), 'utf8');
  if (chunkBytes + b > MAX_BYTES) { yield chunk; chunk = []; chunkBytes = 0; }
  chunk.push(item); chunkBytes += b;
}
if (chunk.length) yield chunk;
```

alice_support: we also recommend instrumenting client to log Content-Length and response status for each chunk — easiest way to correlate with gateway logs.

customer_acme: sounds good. is there any plan to support streaming ingest endpoints so we can send a single stream of NDJSON or a multipart upload?

eng_infra_bot: engineering notes: we have a feature backlog item to support NDJSON streaming for embeddings (ticket INF-7421). current blockers: server-side memory accounting and per-request timeout semantics. potential short-term change: increase edge limit to 20MB for embeddings route only, but that risks OOM for heavy bursts.

sre_liz: safety note: doubling the body limit causes higher memory and cpu spikes during large concurrent jobs. need rate-limiting per-tenant if we bump limit.

alice_support: next steps and owner list: 
- customer_acme: implement client chunking by bytes and add retry/backoff (owner: customer_acme)
- alice_support: draft KB article with recommended chunk sizes and example code (owner: alice_support)
- eng infra: evaluate INF-7421 (streaming NDJSON) and prospect of controlled limit increase + tenant throttling (owner: eng_infra_bot)
- ops_patch: add a log correlation id to embed requests so support can tie client logs -> gateway logs (owner: ops_patch)

customer_acme: will roll out chunking today and report back. thanks for the quick help :thumbsup:

alice_support: awesome — ping here with the first failing chunk and we'll validate logs. if you see dimension mismatches, include raw payload for that chunk (no secrets).

dev_jordan: one last pro tip: if you compress with gzip, set Content-Encoding: gzip and ensure intermediate proxies accept compressed bodies. many edge proxies decompress then re-encode, which can still trip size checks.

customer_acme: noted. I'll implement byte-aware chunking + gzip option and test.

alice_support: closing loop when you confirm success. ticket link: TKT-8743 (support) — will attach notes to the KB.

sre_liz: logged a short-term monitoring alert to catch 413 spike on embeddings route and notify infra on spike > 5/min.

ops_patch: created internal issue: OPS-1910 to add correlation id header for embed requests.

alice_support: thanks everyone. we can reopen thread if new errors pop up. :wave:
